prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Phoenix for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants in Phoenix—“best” depends on your specific case (simple single tooth vs. full-arch, need for grafting/sinus lift), your budget, location, insurance, and comfort with the clinician. I can, however, help you find an excellent provider and tell you how to choose one.

Quick guidance
- For surgical placement, consider an oral & maxillofacial surgeon (OMS) or a periodontist. For the final crown/bridge/prosthesis, a prosthodontist or an experienced restorative dentist is ideal. Some skilled general dentists do both.
- Look for experience (number of implants placed, similar cases), use of CBCT 3D imaging, modern implant systems (Straumann, NobelBiocare, Dentsply Sirona, etc.), and good reviews/referrals.
- Ask for before/after photos and patient references for similar procedures.

Credentials and certifications to look for
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeon: American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (ABOMS) certified.
- Periodontist: American Board of Periodontology certified.
- Prosthodontist: American Board of Prosthodontics certified.
- Memberships: American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID), Academy of Osseointegration.
- Training in implantology (fellowships, continuing education).

Questions to ask at a consultation
- How many implants have you placed? How many like mine?
- Are you board certified? What specialty are you trained in?
- Who will place the implant and who will do the restoration?
- Do you use CBCT imaging and guided surgery?
- What implant system do you use and why?
- What are your success and complication rates?
- Will I need bone grafting or sinus lift? How often do you do those?
- Can I see before/after photos and speak to former patients?
- What is the full cost and financing/warranty policy?

Red flags
- Vague answers about experience or outcomes.
- No 3D imaging (CBCT) for implant planning.
- Extremely low price compared with market without explanation.
- Poor or no reviews and no before/after documentation.
- Pressure to make quick decisions without a written treatment plan.

How I can help now
- If you want, tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and whether you prefer an oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist, or a general dentist who does implants. I can then suggest ways to locate highly rated providers in Phoenix (or a short list of well-reviewed clinics using public directories).
